title: data-labeling-edgecases-guidelines-draft-noah
content:
Scratchpad / notes for label-cleanup pass - edge cases + sample labels Context: - Pulling together examples for next labeling cleanup sprint. Primary goal: reduce inter-annotator variance for intent classification and toxic-content labels. - Working hypotheses: some variance comes from ambiguous prompts, multi-intent examples, and whitespace/encoding artifacts from ingestion. - Related: ML-342 (label drift monitoring), DL-178 (annotation tooling fixes). High-level rules (proposal): 1) Primary-intent-first: if an example clearly contains multiple intents, label with the dominant intent. If tie, mark as multi-intent and route to adjudication. 2) Toxicity: use hierarchical checks - explicit slurs -> TOXIC, strong insults -> TOXIC, ambiguous sarcasm -> POSSIBLY_TOXIC (flag for senior reviewer). 3) NER / slot labels: if token spans overlap, prefer the longer span unless it creates semantic inconsistency. Document examples below. 4) Noise handling: leading/trailing punctuation and repeated-emoji sequences should be normalized before labeling; if normalization would change label, keep original and add a note. Edge cases and example guidance: - Example 1: "Can you book the flight and also tell me the best restaurants?" * Ambiguity: booking vs. recommendation (two intents). * Label: INTENT:multi-intent; Primary: booking (if user mentions booking-related entities like dates/locations). Else adjudicate. - Example 2: "You idiot, get lost" * Strong insult, personal attack. * Label: TOXIC. Add subtag: PERSONAL_ATTACK. - Example 3: "lol that was garbage but the cake was great" * Mixed sentiment. If task is single sentiment label, mark as MIXED_SENTIMENT and provide note: contains positive entity within negative comment. - Example 4: HTML/markup noise: "
Hello
can you help?" * Preprocess: strip tags for content labels but preserve original in metadata. If stripping changes meaning, keep both versions. - Example 5: Non-English + English code-switching: "¿Dónde está the nearest cafe?" * If label set language-specific, mark LANGUAGE:multilingual and route to bilingual annotator. Otherwise annotate intent based on English tokens if majority. Annotation samples (for training the annotators): - "I need a refund for order #12345" -> INTENT:refund; ENT:order_id=#12345 - "This app is trash" -> TOXIC:insult; SENTIMENT:negative - "Book me two tickets to NYC next Friday" -> INTENT:booking; ENT:destination=NYC; ENT:date=next Friday - "I love the new UI :)" -> SENTIMENT:positive; TOXIC:neutral Labeling checklist for cleanup pass: - [ ] Normalize common whitespace and smart-quotes, but keep original text in notes column. - [ ] Flag multi-intent examples as MULTI_INTENT and add short rationale. - [ ] Run regex to find likely order IDs / emails and verify entity extraction labels. - [ ] Review small sample (n=200) of short/one-token examples - high disagreement expected there. - [ ] Add tag "adjudicate" for items where senior reviewer required. Open questions / TODOs: - How to handle implied requests ("Need tickets") where no explicit date/location - should be INTENT:booking + MISSING_ENTITIES tag? (propose yes) - Create a short quick-reference cheat sheet (1p) for crowd annotators - assigned to Asha. - Decide threshold for moving to adjudication: currently thinking >25% annotator disagreement. Feedback? Notes to self: - Check ingestion pipeline for zero-width spaces and weird unicode from iOS copy/paste - saw a spike in Jan that correlated with lower agreement. - Coordinate with Ryan to add a "notes" field to the annotation export so we can preserve preprocessing decisions. - Plan: run pilot (n=1000) with new rules, measure Kappa and label distribution shift vs baseline. Version history: - 2024-01-12: initial scratch notes (Noah) - 2024-01-20: added example bank and checklist (collabs: Asha, Maya) - 2024-02-20: integrated feedback from Ryan about pipeline artifacts; marked for pilot Quick links and references: - Jira: ML-342, DL-178 - Confluence draft: confluence:dl-labeling-guidelines --- Small, messy, and intentionally raw - will turn into a cleaned guideline doc once pilot results are in.
summary: Draft scratchpad: edge-case rules and sample labels for data labeling cleanup pass. Intention: reduce annotator disagreement and create pilot for new rules.
